 "score_claims": "No scores in the README.  "architecture": "One class, one decision function per observation (about 650-710 lines) plus a 325-line map module; the SDK wrapper is the unmodified kit file. No explicit state machine and no planner: a fixed top-to-bottom cascade that sets a move goal, an aim, fire flags and a debug mode label. Order each tick: (1) memory: mech tracks kept 12 s, map of who hit us and when, bearing of last damage, sound bearings (non-far weapon/step/boost/jet sounds) as a threat hint if the last hint is older than 1.5 s; (2) upgrade pick from a fixed priority list; (3) pickup bookkeeping and immediate take when inside pickup radius minus 0.3 m; (4) target = lowest of [horizontal distance + 90 x (hp/1400) + 30 x seconds since seen, minus 50 if it hit us in the last 3 s, minus 40 if it was our target in the last 2 s] over every track seen within 4 s, with no distance cap and no engagement gate; (5) threat count = tracks seen within 3 s and within 160 m (includes the target); (6) zone goal; (7) if a target exists: aim/fire plus fight movement (retreat if \"losing\", otherwise range-keeping with strafing), then cube/weapon detours (5.19 version); when outside the zone the fight move is dropped in favour of the zone goal while still shooting; (8) heal state if no target, no zone goal, no move goal; (9) else zone goal; (10) else a single min-score loot list, else roam toward the next circle; (11) movement execution through straight line or distance field; (12) projectile dodge overlay; (13) stuck handling; (14) idle aim scan; (15) laser hold and reload housekeeping; (16) spend leftover time on the path field. The main-branch line additionally has a permanent free-for-all flag that switches on selective engagement, hiding and endgame camping; the 5.19 version has no such flag at all and always fights.",
 "navigation": "Ground only. Map preprocessing: 1 m raster of terrain height plus, per cell, the highest prism top and lowest prism base (one solid column per cell). Nav grid of 2 m cells (1070 x 724 m map, about 194k cells): a cell is walkable if no cell in a 6 x 6 m window has a prism rising more than 1.2 m above ground with its base lower than 9.5 m above ground, the terrain differs by at most 2.2 m to the cells 2 m east and north, and it is not on the map edge. Body size is fixed (no growth with cubes). Path finding is a whole-map 8-connected Dijkstra distance field grown outward from the goal (uniform cost, no corner cutting, no danger cost), time-sliced over ticks: goals are keyed to a 5 m lattice, a running computation is not restarted for a new goal within 25 m, an unwalkable goal snaps to the nearest walkable cell within 60 m. Steering reads the last finished field: sample 24 headings out to 5 cells along straight walkable rays and head for the lowest value. Per tick: if the goal is within 60 m and a sampled sight line at 2 m height is clear, walk straight; otherwise use the field if it was built for a goal within 25 m (30 m when chasing a target), else walk straight anyway. Per-tick budget for the field: 8 ms minus time used (main) or 20 ms minus time used with a hard cap of 70,000 node expansions (5.19 version, made deterministic). Two full field builds at init warm the JIT. Line of sight = sampling the segment every 1 m against the raster (terrain and prisms only; trees and canopy ignored). Cover search: 16 directions on rings every 6 m out to 36-50 m around a point; a candidate must be walkable and hidden from the enemy eye (enemy feet + 8 m) to our torso (ground + 6 m); score = ring radius minus 0.3 x extra distance gained from the enemy. Stuck: commanded to move but displaced under 0.25 m per decision while grounded for 0.6 s leads to jump plus boost; after 2.5 s rotate the move 90 degrees; reset at 4 s; boost (jet) while airborne if stuck. No deliberate roof or jet use; loot more than 2 m above terrain is ignored.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Aim point = target feet + 4.5 m x target size scale. Gun: three fixed-point iterations of a first-order intercept using the track's last velocity, extrapolated by track age plus flight time (vertical velocity capped to 0.3 s); no acceleration or strafe-pattern model. Gun fires whenever the target was seen this tick, raster sight line is clear, distance is under gun range (so out to 230 m), yaw error versus the gun's lead solution is under 1.2 x atan(2.2 m x scale / distance), pitch error under twice that plus 0.03, and the gun is not reloading. Torso aim priority: direct (no lead) when lightning is held and the target is within 1.1 x its range, or when a laser is held and is charging or within 0.2 s of ready; otherwise the gun lead. Lightning: fire when distance < range minus 1 m, yaw error < 0.45 x cone angle, energy above one shot's cost + 2. Laser: start charging when off cooldown, target seen this tick, within laser range, and either sight line clear or distance < 60 m (pre-charge behind cover); keep holding until charge is within 0.05 s of full, then release only when aligned (yaw error < 0.9 x tolerance, pitch < 1.5 x tolerance + 0.02) with sight line clear; keeps charging to full if the target is briefly lost. Mortar: only between 18 and 220 m and off cooldown; leads with a crude flight time (distance / 0.7 x shell speed), solves the ballistic angle from a launch height 9.5 m x scale, uses the low arc with sight line and the high arc without (indirect fire over buildings), takes over the aim only on ticks when neither slot is firing and no laser is charging, fires within 0.03 rad. Reload: manual reload only outside pure fight mode (roam, loot, heal, retreat) when under half a magazine; in a fight it relies on the automatic reload. Crates and drones: nearest visible drone within 110 m, else crate within 120 m, simple lead at 252 m/s, tolerance atan(1.2 / distance), gun plus lightning under 40 m; suppressed when HP < 40% or a mech hit us in the last 1.5 s.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Practice-mode philosophy of the 5.19 version: kill fast and snowball, do not hide. It engages every mech seen in the last 4 s at any range, prefers the nearest, weakest, freshest track, with strong bias to whoever just hit it and to its current target (focus fire, finish kills). Stand-off distance by loadout: about 28 m with lightning (boost in when 43-90 m away and energy > 70), about 110 m with laser, about 70 m gun-only, with a +/-15 m dead band (approach at full input, back off at 0.7). Constant strafe at 0.9 lateral input, direction re-rolled randomly every 0.35-1.05 s. If the target has neither been seen this tick nor has a sight line, path toward it. Enemy laser: if the target is charging and its yaw is within 0.25 rad of us, boost-strafe (energy > 10, or > 45 when carrying lightning); in practice it deliberately does not run for cover (author: squad focus fire made cover-seeking too passive). \"Losing\" = not finishing (target under 20% HP, we over 20%, at most 2 threats) and one of: own HP < 35% with the target's HP fraction at least 0.1 above ours; 2+ threats with HP < 55%; 3+ threats with HP < 80%. When losing: boost (energy > 15) to the best cover spot within 50 m from the target (or straight away), still shooting when aligned. Heal state: needs no track seen for 4 s and no zone pressure; triggers at HP < 55% (or < 90% for 6 s after last losing); stands still and silent, or if the last-seen mech could see it, creeps at 0.4 move input (about 4.7 m/s, below the 5 m/s step-sound threshold) to cover within 36 m; torso keeps rotating to scan. Other: 360 degree spin in the first 3 s after spawn; when hit by an unseen mech turn to the damage bearing for 2 s; otherwise look at the latest sound/damage bearing for 3 s, else sweep +/-0.9 rad around the heading. Dodging: gun bullets whose closest approach within 0.9 s is under 3.6 m x scale trigger a sidestep perpendicular to the bullet path; mortar shells predicted to land within 3 s and within 11 m of our extrapolated position trigger a move directly away; dodge blends 0.3 old move + 0.95 dodge and boosts if energy > 25 (55 when holding lightning with a target). Nothing specific for the single early hunter or the late all-in hunt; late game is the same fight/retreat logic.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "5.19 version: weapon values laser 3.2, lightning 2.5, mortar 1, gun 0; the gun is never dropped; an empty slot takes anything; a held non-gun weapon is swapped only for one worth more than 0.5 higher (so lightning or mortar are replaced by laser; a charging laser is never swapped). End loadout tends to gun + laser. Upgrade priority: plating (+15% max HP), armor (-8% damage), nanites (regen), then lightning efficiency, laser damage, laser charge, gun damage, gun rate, lightning range/chain, gyros, servos, gun magazine, capacitor, reactor, jets, gun velocity, sensors, mortar items, laser pierce last. Memory: ground-level cubes remembered 40 s and ground-level weapon pickups 60 s (forgotten when we come within 18 m and no longer see them, or on take events). Mid-fight economy (the change that made the 5.19 version): during a fight the move goal is overridden to the nearest remembered cube if it is within 70 m (HP > 50%), 40 m (HP lower) or 12 m (while losing); else to a wanted weapon within 60 m if holding only the gun, 35 m otherwise (not while losing). Healing is skipped while a cube is within 40 m. Out of fight, one min-score list: wanted weapon = distance minus 20 x value (minus another 50 if gun-only); cube = distance minus 30; supply drop = distance minus 80 if within 220 m, not held by another mech, reachable by landing time + 3 s and not outside the next circle with under 15 s to shrink (stands still once inside ring radius minus 3 m); drone (HP > 50%, remembered up to 25 s with HP tracked from our own hits, within 170 m) = distance minus 20, approach to 38 m then stand and shoot; ground crate (HP > 45%, within 150 m) = distance + 5, approach to 30 m, walk onto it under 25 m. Roof loot (more than 2 m above terrain) is ignored. Main-branch differences: values lightning 3, laser 2.6 (those two never replace each other), armor before plating, no cube/weapon memory and no mid-fight pickup.",
 "zone_and_endgame": "Zone goal is active when outside the zone, or beyond 90% of the current radius, or when farther than 80% of the next radius from the next centre and either the circle is shrinking or time-to-shrink is less than walk time to 60% of the next radius plus 12 s. The goal is the point at 45% of the next radius on our own side of the next centre. When not fighting it outranks looting and disables healing; boost only when outside the zone with energy > 20. In a fight the zone only takes over when we are actually outside (fight movement is dropped, shooting continues). Roaming default: drift to min(60% of next radius, max(20, distance to centre minus 30)) on our side. No special endgame in the 5.19 version: no last-circle logic, no out-healing or damage-race reasoning, it simply converges on the centre and keeps fighting. Main-branch only, and only after the free-for-all flag is set: with 6 or fewer alive, HP > 40% and nobody engaged, it sits in a cover spot (35 m search) near min(55% of next radius, max(12, distance minus 15)) on its side, shielded from the nearest track of the last 8 s or the last threat bearing, facing that direction.",
 "housebot_observations": "Very little written down. Two statements by the author: (1) practice house bots never fight each other, which is the basis of the free-for-all detector (three or more deaths not caused by us, or two sightings of a laser/lightning beam that ends on another mech and does not pass within 20 m of us); (2) in practice the squad focus-fires, and breaking line of sight when a laser charges at us made the bot too passive there, so that behaviour is gated to free-for-all. Implied by the version history: a version that never fights and only evades from spawn through cover was committed at 22:30 ET and replaced by the restored 5.19 fighter at 22:40 ET, consistent with the spec's reading that practice score is roughly kills before death. Third-party note (Achintya-Lakshmanan report in our intel): practice rank 1-4 bots including Wolverines averaged about 6th-12th place in a top-16 free-for-all showdown, so this practice-tuned style did not transfer directly.",
 "measured_lessons": [
  "Official practice 5.19 (receipt BB-098D02A6) was achieved by 'v8-econ': the always-fight base plus mid-fight cube pickup with cube memory, remembered weapon pickups, laser valued above lightning (3.2 vs 2.5), plating ahead of armor in the upgrade order. The author names this the '5.19 economy bot' in two later commit titles.",
  "After 5.19 the author tried (exp v9) 'fight isolation' (shift 6-18 m to a spot that non-target enemies cannot see), laser dodge to cover sized by remaining charge time, and a wider lightning firing cone (0.45 -> 0.8 of cone angle), each behind an environment-variable switch for ablation. The next version (v10) was rebuilt from the 5.19 code without any of the three; no score is recorded, but none was kept (inference: they did not beat 5.19).",
  "v10 = 5.19 bot + flee to 75 m from any remembered drone within 58 m when HP < 50%; no score recorded; the author then restored plain 5.19 rather than v10.",
  "A pure-evasion build (never targets mechs; from the first tick moves to cover from the nearest mech within 150 m, or 55 m straight away, zone route winning when needed) was committed 22:30 ET and reverted to the 5.19 fighter at 22:40 ET; no number given.",
  "Local free-for-all A/B (author's own simulator, not the official scorer): not shooting crates/drones while any mech was tracked within 6 s and 200 m ('gunfire reveals position') scored about 9.6 versus about 8.0 before.",
  "Local free-for-all A/B: with 6 or fewer alive and not engaged, holding cover inside the next circle instead of roaming gave about +0.8 over the silence-only version across two seed ranges; gated to free-for-all so practice is unaffected.",
  "Local free-for-all A/B: seeking cover (while still firing) when the target charges a laser at us gave about +0.76 over the previous version across three seed ranges; explicitly free-for-all only because in practice 'squad focus-fire made cover-seek too passive'.",
  "Third-party (r1ver notes): two independent derivatives of v8-econ scored 5.08 and 5.10 on the official scorer; in r1ver's local 32-seed test their 'pick cube piles by upgrade value' variant was 0.56 below unmodified v8-econ, and 0.13 lower per match over 8 mirrored free-for-all seeds.",
  "Third-party (r1ver local model, seeds 4101-4116): the older TTUN v7 (the free-for-all-detecting line that is on main) scored 1.688 in their practice model versus 4.563 for their control, and tied at 12.125 in their free-for-all model; treat as their simulator only.",
  "Engineering: the path-field time slice was changed from wall-clock only (8 ms) to 20 ms with a fixed cap of 70,000 expansions per tick so that behaviour is reproducible under CPU contention."

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Economy during combat: remember cubes for 40 s and detour to them mid-fight with HP-dependent radii (70 / 40 / 12 m); skip healing when a cube is within 40 m. This is the single change tied to the best official score.",
  "Kills as the cube source: a duel-branch refinement closes to 14 m on a target under 38% HP (own HP > 42%, at most 2 threats; 50 m if it has lightning and we do not), boosting when energy > 65, so the dropped cubes are collected immediately.",
  "Loadout-aware duel range (duel branch): about 128 m with laser, 92 m gun-only, 27 m with lightning; close to 28 m against a mortar holder and 35 m against a laser holder when we have no laser; stay at 70 m or more against lightning when we have none.",
  "Practice-versus-free-for-all detector from unexplained deaths (alive count versus own kills) and beams ending on other mechs, used to switch between an aggressive and a selective/hiding personality.",
  "Whole-map Dijkstra distance field from the goal, time-sliced across ticks with JIT warm-up at init; steering by sampling 24 rays of 10 m over the finished field; a deterministic expansion cap per tick.",
  "Silent healing: creep at 40% move input (under the 5 m/s step-sound threshold) to a spot hidden from the last-seen enemy, then stand still.",
  "Laser pre-charge without sight line when the target is within 60 m, release only when fully charged and aligned; keep the charge if the target is lost for a moment.",
  "High-arc mortar fire when there is no sight line, low arc otherwise.",
  "Energy reserve: higher boost thresholds for dodging when carrying lightning (45 / 55 instead of 10 / 25) so the arc weapon is never starved.",
  "Reading the enemy 'charging' flag plus yaw alignment to us as a laser warning; in the dropped experiment the cover search radius was sized by time left in the charge (clamped 6-18 m at boost speed) and own laser charging was not started while running.",
  "Fight isolation scoring (dropped): among 16 directions at 6/12/18 m choose the spot seen by the fewest non-target enemies (+100 each), prefer keeping the target visible (+25 if lost), +1.5 per metre.",
  "Drone memory with HP tracked from own hit events, and (v10) leaving a drone's reach when HP < 50%.",
  "Environment-variable switches inside the bot for fast ablations, and a publish script that syncs the bot to a dedicated submission branch."
 ],
 "apparent_weaknesses": [
  "The public main/submit code is not the best-scoring version; anyone copying main gets the free-for-all line without the economy changes (and with lightning-first, armor-first).",
  "No engagement gate and gun fire out to 230 m with a first-order lead: low hit rate on strafing targets at range, constant gun noise, empty magazines at bad moments (no reload in lulls while a target is tracked).",
  "Only reacts to one enemy: cover and retreat are computed against the current target; other squad members' sight lines are ignored (the multi-enemy isolation attempt was dropped).",
  "Retreat triggers late in a 1v1 (own HP < 35%) and healing stops at 55% HP (the 90% clause expires 6 s after the last losing tick); healing also needs 4 s with no track at all and is disabled whenever a zone goal is active.",
  "Fight movement is pure radial + strafe geometry with a 10 m look-ahead and no obstacle awareness; it strafes into walls and relies on the jump/boost stuck handler.",
  "Sight-line model ignores trees and canopy and collapses each cell to one solid column (lowest base to highest top), so it shoots into trunks and misjudges overhangs, bridges and stacked prisms.",
  "Walkability uses the base body size only; with many cubes (up to +50% size) the mech can wedge in gaps the grid thinks are open.",
  "Uniform-cost path field with a single pending goal: goals more than 25 m apart restart the whole-map search, so alternating goals (target, cube, loot) can leave it walking straight lines into geometry for several ticks.",
  "Per-tick path work of up to 20 ms on top of decision logic is aggressive against a 50 ms limit under CPU contention.",
  "Target HP term is normalised by a fixed 1400 instead of the target's max HP; stale tracks (up to 4 s) still drive movement.",
  "Drone farming parks at 38 m, inside the 45 m aggro radius, and the 5.19 version has no drone avoidance when hurt.",
  "No endgame plan for the shrinking final circle (no positioning for the last zone, no out-lasting logic); no roof play, so the 25% of floor loot on roofs is never collected.",
  "Main-branch free-for-all detector can false-trigger in practice if three house bots die to zone or drones, flipping the bot into selective/hiding mode late in a practice match.",
  "Supply-drop capture does not check for other mechs inside the ring and is only considered when no target is tracked.",
  "Mortar lead uses a rough flight-time guess and only fires when aligned within 0.03 rad, so it rarely fires at moving targets; the laser's 110 m stand-off halves movement while charging with no peek-from-cover behaviour in practice."
 ]
